newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan securities watchdog chairman to visit China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan securities watchdog chairman to visit China.

text.p: The chairman of Taiwan's top securities watchdog said on Monday he would attend an international conference in Beijing and follow up with a visit to arch rival China's main stock exchange in Shanghai.

Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Lu Tung-ying said in a statement he would participate in an April 15-20 annual meeting of the International Organisation of Securities Commissions in Beijing.
Participants from the 20-strong organisation would discuss management of Asia-Pacific stock markets and promote regional cooperation.
Lu planned to visit the Shanghai Stock Exchange in his private capacity after the conference, but his statement gave no further details.

Nationalist-ruled Taiwan has prohibited direct official contacts with communist China since a civil war split them in 1949, but officials are allowed to attend international conferences or visit in their private capacities.
Senior Beijing officials have visited Taiwan in rapidly increasing numbers in recent years despite a freeze in semi-official talks imposed by Beijing during a period of intense friction in mid-1995.
